The action invokes Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, citing Canadian provincial and territorial bans on U.S. alcoholic beverages implemented beginning March 2025. Trump found that Canada discriminated against U.S. commerce while not restricting beverages from other countries, causing U.S. exports to Canada to fall 81 percent. The proclamation authorizes the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection to implement the tariffs and modify the Harmonized Tariff Schedule accordingly.

events.title: FDA Revokes Color Additive Listing for Orange B
events.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a final order revoking the color additive listing for Orange B, previously used for coloring the casings or surfaces of frankfurters and sausages. The resolution, proposed by Democrat Pramila Jayapal, passed with support from all Democrats and four Republicans (Tom Barrett, Warren Davidson, Thomas Massie, Brian Fitzpatrick). This follows an identical resolution passed in June that was also approved by the Senate. The Trump administration has argued war powers resolutions are unconstitutional and has not complied with the prior Senate-approved resolution.
events.why_relevant: The passage represents Congress asserting its constitutional war powers authority against executive defiance, with the Trump administration refusing to comply with a prior bipartisan Senate-approved resolution, raising fundamental separation-of-powers questions.
events.basis: The US House of Representatives for the second time passed a war powers resolution directing Donald Trump to withdraw the US military from the conflict with Iran.

events.title: Senate declines to advance joint resolution to end Iran War hostilities
events.summary: The Senate declined to advance Senate Joint Resolution 180, sponsored by Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), which would have forced the president to end U.S. hostilities with Iran. The measure failed by a vote of 47 to 49, with four Republican senators not voting. Unlike the House concurrent resolution, a joint resolution is a law requiring presidential signature and is typically used for urgent matters such as declarations of war. Senators used the joint resolution mechanism because such resolutions are privileged in the Senate.

events.title: Complaint filed: Electronic Privacy Information Center v. Mullin (S.D. Cal.)
events.summary: The Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC) and three U.S. citizens filed a complaint in the Southern District of California against the Department of Homeland Security, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, and other immigration enforcement officials, alleging that DHS maintains an unpublished "Protester Surveillance Policy" that collects and retains personally identifying information on Americans engaged in observation and protest of immigration enforcement. events.summary: The Food and Drug Administration issued a final debarment order on July 24, 2026, prohibiting Francis Esteban Matos from importing or offering for import any drug into the United States for five years. events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency issued a final Significant New Use Rule (SNUR) under the Toxic Substances Control Act for multi-walled carbon nanotubes (PMN P-22-163). events.title: Trump imposes new tariffs on 80+ countries citing forced labor
events.summary: At 12:01 a.m. on July 24, Trump imposed tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% on goods from more than 80 countries representing 99.4% of U.S. trade, claiming the countries produce goods using forced labor. The action invokes a different legal authority than the "Liberation Day" tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court in February 2026 and differs from tariffs imposed after that ruling. events.why_relevant: Imposing tariffs under a different legal theory immediately after the Supreme Court invalidated prior tariffs suggests an attempt to circumvent judicial review and constitutional limits on executive economic power.

events.title: American universities reduced academic standards through grade inflation to maintain enrollment growth
events.summary: Research cited in the article found that most increases in college graduation rates since the 1990s resulted from grade inflation rather than improved student preparation or institutional resources. Universities implemented higher grades while holding exam performance constant, enabling degree completion without mastery of material. This practice allowed colleges to expand enrollment while maintaining graduation statistics as they attempted to serve as America's primary unifying institution.
events.why_relevant: Grade inflation undermines the credibility and signaling function of university degrees, degrading the quality of human capital production and the institution's capacity to serve as a reliable educational and social institution.
events.federal_nexus: Universities receive federal research funding and federal student loan programs depend on degree completion rates.
